page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture operating at a base speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an extensive 480 MB L3 cache alongside instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded throughput in compression workloads, achieving 34.67 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.51 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, placing in the top quartile. However, multi-core and memory throughput reflect constraints typical of lower core counts. Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 4032.62 and multi-threaded bzip3 reached 28.21 GB/sec, placing in the lower quartile. Memory write bandwidth for large 256 MB blocks measured 22.85 GB/sec, while read bandwidth registered 44.91 GB/sec. In application metrics, the instance handled 7.49 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.32 GB/sec in static web serving, both within median thresholds. CPU-bound machine learning tasks on medium models showed limited throughput, recording 4.97 tokens per second for 7B parameter text generation.

The balanced resource configuration offers cost efficiency for workloads that do not demand extensive core concurrency or integrated local disk arrays. Given its lack of local storage, persistent disk performance relies on attached network volumes. The D4s_v7 is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, including standard web serving, small-scale caching layers, light database services, and single-threaded data transformation tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D4s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor on Microsoft Hyper-V. Based on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, coupled with 16.0 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 ratio. The CPU incorporates 480 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX acceleration extensions. The instance provisions no discrete GPU hardware and no bundled local storage, requiring remote storage for persistence. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 34.67 GB/sec, alongside average results in static web serving at 8.32 GB/sec and Redis operations at 7.49 million operations per second. Conversely, multi-threaded scaling and memory write bandwidth sit in lower tiers due to core constraints. The D4s_v7 offers balanced resource density suited for general-purpose enterprise tasks, mid-tier web serving, Redis caching, and microservices architectures.
